@[expose] public section

open EuclideanGeometry

namespace Erdos93

/--
If $n$ distinct points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ form a convex polygon then they determine at least
$\lfloor \frac{n}{2}\rfloor$ distinct distances.

Solved by Altman [Al63].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1d7b3f00780b85ed0462e79a1cd5650ee9055655/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos93.lean"]
theorem erdos_93 (A : Finset ℝ²) (hA : ConvexIndep (A : Set ℝ²)) :
    A.card / 2 ≤ distinctDistances A := by
  sorry

end Erdos93

reformulations.difference: The Lean theorem includes convex-independent finite sets with fewer than three points, whereas the source describes the vertices of a convex polygon.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The additional cases are automatic: with zero or one point both the required floor and the distance count are zero; two distinct points determine exactly one distance, meeting floor(2/2)=1. Thus the universal assertion is equivalent to its restriction to cardinality at least three. This equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, independently of erdos_93. The scratch file also proves the rephrasing with an explicit n, Mathlib's ConvexIndependent, and Nat.floor ((n : ℝ) / 2).

review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully states the source's bound. Checked that ℝ² uses Euclidean distance, ConvexIndep expresses convex position, and distinctDistances counts distinct nonzero pairwise lengths. Scratch checks compile without errors and the equivalence proofs have no sorryAx. The research solved and formal_proof records agree with the source. The linked proof has matching hypotheses and conclusion after the checked equivalences and contains no sorry or custom axioms; its older-toolchain project was not independently rebuilt. Full text of the five later surveys Er90, Er92e, Er95, Er97e, and Er97f was not obtained; their bibliography entries were checked. The online statement and the accessible primary sources suffice to settle the declaration's faithfulness.
